utterances.text: Your Honour, the transcript issue, page 78, line -- beginning at line 7. And it was when I asked him about these persons who are listed in P2329, he said they were made prisoners and taken to Vecici. And were kept there in order to reap the corn. And I'm told that what he said where you see those dashes is that they were actually put on the tractors and basically used as, as I understood it, they were put on the tractors to keep the Serbs from shooting while they were doing the harvest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Sadikovic, you have heard what Mr. Ackerman has just stated. Do you confirm that that is what you stated earlier on? Because we have it missing from the transcript. Answer yes or no, because we have already gone beyond our time limit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct. That's what I was told. That was why they had been taken to Vecici, for that reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That brings your testimony to an end, which basically means that you are now free to go back home. Mr. Usher will accompany you out of this courtroom, and other officials of this Tribunal will assist you to make it easy for you to return back home at the earliest possible time. On my part, on behalf of Judge Taya, Judge Janu, I should like to thank you for having come over here, and on behalf of everyone, I would like to wish you a safe journey back home, and happy birthday too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours. I wish you every luck in your further work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We can adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just before we do adjourn, Your Honour, I know it's running over time slightly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How long will this take?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. I think -- two minutes. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's simply this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We're talking it from discussions yesterday and discussions I've had with Mr. Ackerman that Mr. Treanor will not be cross-examined when he gives evidence next week, and Mr. Brown when he gives evidence the week after. Accordingly, we're allowing one day for each of these witnesses in chief, and we're moving witnesses up at speed. Your Honour, any witness lists Your Honours may have had, or indeed Mr. Ackerman, are now moot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can update us on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But I merely point that -- so that is the situation as I understand it, and as we're taking it and any further change is going to cause complete chaos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. Definitely we're not going to make things more difficult for you, Ms. Korner. I mean, it's -- we are not unreasonable.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the other thing is Mr. Druzic, he can't come -- we will try to get him for this Monday. He has to come back to finish cross-examination. He can come back for the 7th of July, but Mr. Cunningham isn't going to be here, because he's in the States. However, I'm told by Mr. Cunningham there shouldn't be a problem and that somebody else can complete the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But Monday, who will be coming on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This coming Monday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The witness who Your Honour has granted delayed disclosure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. We can adjourn -- do you have any comments on what has been communicated to us by Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think it's all accurate, Your Honour, and with regard to Druzic, I think we can deal with that. If your negotiations were successful at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm hopeful. We're hopeful. So I thank you, and we are adjourning until tomorrow. Tomorrow I think you're taking over the witness, no, Mr. Cunningham?

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. We're moving out. Can I have a word with you, Mr. Ackerman, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
